title: Token Corridor Competitive Decision-Control Plane
mission: Define and prove an OSS-first, provider-neutral bounded-decision control plane (working name Token Corridor) inside the AgentSwitchboard software factory. Before inventing infrastructure, evaluate real open/self-hosted decision engines, routers, structured-output runtimes, durable workflow engines, agent runtimes, sandboxes, and eval/observability platforms against commercial comparators. Compile repository/runtime evidence into typed decision requests, choose the cheapest adequate open or commercial engine by measured policy, preserve calibrated uncertainty and authority provenance, and route execution without duplicating Prompt Kit, FirstMate, AgentSwitchboard execution adapters, or already-solved open-source infrastructure.

acceptanceCriteria: At least one credible open/self-hosted candidate is investigated for every major software-factory substrate layer before local implementation is proposed.
Jev is treated as one closed comparator in a broader decision-engine field, not an assumed dependency.
License class is explicit: permissive open source, copyleft open source, source-available, or closed/managed.
Structured-output tools are separated from calibrated decision models; model routers are separated from execution adapters; workflow durability is separated from agent runtime.
Private products occupy the comparison matrix but cannot become required infrastructure merely because they are polished or managed.

Local owners remain explicit: Prompt Kit policy/semantics; Token Corridor bounded decision composition; AgentSwitchboard execution/evidence control; FirstMate live crew runtime; NodeWeaver optional signal source.
Claims remain evidence-typed and vendor/self-reported performance is not promoted to local workload proof.

inputs: Prompt Kit Evidence Spine continuation and authority semantics
TC-00A selected open decision backend and challenger

acceptanceCriteria: Decision state/evidence, action authority, and execution state are mechanically separate.
Request binds a stable state/action fingerprint and expected typed question shape.
Receipt records engine identity/version, probability/confidence, calibration provenance when available, latency/cost when observable, disposition, and proof ceiling.
Unknown/low-confidence paths abstain or escalate instead of fabricating certainty.
Authorization originates only from typed upstream grant/policy/owner evidence; no model output can create it.
The first proven runtime path uses an open/local backend; commercial adapters remain optional.
The interface allows Jev, open System-One engines, NLI/classifier engines, constrained local LLMs, specialist routers, and deterministic code without changing downstream factory contracts.

proof.target: Durable OSS-first competitive architecture plan narrowing the open and managed decision/software-factory ecosystem into evidence-gated Token Corridor and AgentSwitchboard development.
proof.achieved: The initial Jev-centric research floor was found incomplete and corrected. Current plan now inventories open/self-hosted and managed alternatives across decision engines, model routing, structured generation, durability, sandbox/runtime, software-factory orchestration, and eval/observability; exact local runtime bakeoffs remain unproven.
proof.ceiling: This plan proves a source-backed open-vs-managed architecture and selection program only. It does not prove any candidate's performance on the user's factory corpus, production readiness on the user's hardware, Token Corridor runtime behavior, live AFK execution, or a standalone product/repository boundary.
